title: Why You Hear Voices When Nobody Is There
hook: You sometimes hear phantom sounds, even when completely alone.

narration.text: You sometimes hear phantom sounds, even when completely alone.
This is often your brain trying to make sense of silence.
It anticipates sounds, based on past experiences and expectations.
Sometimes, these expectations create a sound that is not really there.
Your brain fills the void with a "best guess" sound.
It could be a faint voice, a doorbell, or footsteps nearby.
This happens more when you are tired or highly focused.
It is a normal brain function, not a cause for concern.
Have you ever heard a sound that was not there?

description: Ever heard a faint sound or voice when you are completely alone? It is not spooky, it is your brain playing tricks. Your mind anticipates sounds, sometimes creating phantom noises out of silence.
topic: Why you sometimes 'hear' voices or sounds that are not there when you are alone, explaining auditory hallucinations and expectation.
